title: A shop beyond the souvenir
speaker: tenant_salmah
dialogue: My regular customers come for cloth, advice and someone who remembers what they need. But in this imagined future, the next lease is harder to afford. An apprentice needs time to learn, and the rent cannot wait, you know. How do we keep this a working shop, not just somewhere to visit?
question: Protect the lease, fund an apprentice, or invest in shared ownership?
options: Keep independent traders in place, with owner compensation.
Pay for skills to be taught; rent pressure remains.
Put premises into shared ownership at a high upfront cost.
consequence: Rent relief buys time. Apprenticeships preserve practice. Shared ownership needs capacity that could fund other needs.

title: Who ties the next garland?
speaker: custodian_rahim
dialogue: A flower garland is made by hand. The rhythm, you learn by sitting beside someone. Around Campbell Lane, our imagined workshop needs time to teach and orders to fill also. A photo can show the finished garland, but who will pay for the hours of learning?
question: Support teaching, secure a home for it, or adapt another space?
options: Fund mentoring and time to practise.
Bring an old unit into use while retaining its archive.
consequence: An archive protects records, while active teaching sustains continuity. More commercial demand can still displace learners.

title: The hands missing from the record
speaker: custodian_rahim
dialogue: In this future, our teaching chain has broken already. We still have photos and oral histories, but fewer people who can guide a learner. New funding can protect what is left. It cannot bring every lost skill back just like that.
question: Rebuild teaching, secure long-term space, or protect surviving records?
options: Rebuild practice gradually; lost knowledge limits recovery.
Secure space for a long commitment.
Keep surviving records inside a newly used space.
consequence: Once continuity crosses the lasting-loss threshold, grants cannot instantly restore it.

title: Space around a living temple
speaker: youth_faiz
dialogue: Around Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple, people come to pray, work and visit. Older neighbours need comfortable access. People need room to gather also, without blocking the way. Can visitor income help the neighbourhood while respecting the temple?
question: Share visitor income, support nearby community premises, or invest in learning?
options: Support community ownership of nearby premises.
Raise funds and distribute benefits, with a ten-year sunset.
Make learning and participation more viable.
consequence: A busy district does not automatically share its gains. Equity needs direct support.

title: Beyond the colourful photograph
place: Former House of Tan Teng Niah · Kerbau Road
speaker: operator_jo
dialogue: People stop to take photos of the Former House of Tan Teng Niah. But the walk around it needs shade and somewhere to rest, especially for older people and those working nearby. Can we improve the space around it? The heritage house itself, we must look after, lah.
question: Cool nearby buildings, improve shade and walking access, or raise shared funds?
options: Add shade and walking space while retaining a loading window.
Fund community improvements, with a sunset review.
consequence: Cooling directly improves habitability. Pedestrianisation also attracts activity and can increase rent pressure.

title: Who benefits from the footfall?
speaker: operator_jo
dialogue: Shopping around Mustafa Centre brings customers here. But crowded does not mean the small shops and late-night workers all benefit, right? Should we protect the tenants, share the visitor income, or put more into evening business?
question: Redistribute benefits, protect traders, or expand evening activity?
options: Share visitor income, accepting some loss of demand.
Protect existing traders from rising rent pressure.
Bring more evening activity, with a quiet-hours agreement.
consequence: High vitality alongside weak continuity can lock the district into visitor monoculture.

title: A story with room to continue
speaker: custodian_rahim
dialogue: The Indian Heritage Centre keeps stories of our communities. Nearby, our imagined workshop needs a place where the skills can still be practised. If a shophouse gets a new use, will there be room for teaching and community memories also?
question: Support reuse of nearby shophouses, invest in teaching, or secure community premises?
options: Allow new activity with an archive protection clause.
Fund living practice instead of a display alone.
consequence: Reuse brings activity but may increase rent pressure. Records alone do not keep a living practice alive.

title: Keep the market working
speaker: tenant_salmah
dialogue: At Tekka Centre, you buy groceries, have a meal and see a familiar face, all in one day. In this imagined future, our food business wants more evening trade. But staff need rest, deliveries need access, and the streets must stay comfortable also. What would make the extra business worthwhile?
question: Extend evenings, improve comfort, or make room for walking?
options: Expand evening activity with a noise curfew.
Improve walking and shade with delivery access.
consequence: A curfew reduces some harms; it does not remove the long-term trade-offs of night activity.

title: A place to spend a day off
speaker: youth_faiz
dialogue: Some people come here to meet friends on their day off. Others live nearby and want a shared space everyone looks after. To sit down and feel welcome, you should not have to buy something, right? How can we fund places where people can just gather?
question: Share visitor income, support community premises, or fund the next generation?
options: Support community ownership of nearby premises.
Raise funds and distribute benefits, with a ten-year sunset.
Make learning and participation more viable.
consequence: A busy district does not automatically share its gains. Equity needs direct support.
